To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The redesign of business processes is a necessary condition for effective e-commerce and that the best practices for BPR are a good starting point for the redesign of business processes to support e-commerce".

(i) BPR best practices are useful to redesign business processes to support e-commerce; (ii) BPR best practice implementation leads to reduced lead times; (iii) the reduction of lead time is not a direct function of the amount of BPR best practices implemented, but rather of the amount of best practices that are relevant for a given business process.
e-commerce is not just about the Internet, but about the redesign of business processes to achieve the presumed business benefits.

the redesign of business processes to support the e-commerce strategy.
the question how to design business processes for e-commerce.
the question: how can business processes be redesigned to support effective e-commerce?

the best practices for BPR, which were developed for the traditional business world, are applicable to redesign processes for the e-business world as well.
the best practices for BPR are applicable for e-commerce and can be applied to redesign existing processes.
the application of BPR best practices in the context of the service industry can lead to a reduction of lead times.

BPR can be applied successfully to e-commerce, but that the application of best practice is not sufficient for a successful e-commerce implementation.
the best practice approach for BPR is a useful tool for the redesign of business processes in the e-commerce context, as it is for the traditional business context.
e-commerce requires a rethinking and reengineering of the existing business processes.

e-commerce can be successfully implemented if business process redesign is done right.
